subject: Civil Engineering
title: Dam Stability Analysis
description: Learn Dam Stability Analysis in one minute.

hook.text: A dam can fail by sliding, overturning, or overstressing — each must be checked independently.

buildup.text: Sliding resistance compares friction and cohesion at the base against horizontal water force.

discovery.text: Overturning stability checks that the dam's weight keeps the resultant force inside the base.

twist.text: Safety factors of 1.5 to 3.0 are required — the dam must be far stronger than minimally stable.

climax.text: Multiple load cases — normal, flood, earthquake, post-earthquake — each gets its own analysis.

punchline.text: A dam must pass every test. One failure mode is all it takes to bring it down.

quiz.question: What does overturning stability analysis check for a dam?
options: Whether the dam can withstand wind forces from behind
That the dam's weight keeps the resultant force within the base, preventing rotation
Whether the dam's concrete will crack during temperature changes

details.summary: Dam stability analysis evaluates whether the structure can safely resist overturning, sliding, and overstressing under all loading conditions. Engineers calculate factors of safety by comparing stabilizing forces like dam weight to destabilizing forces like water pressure.
details.whyItMatters: Stability analysis is the core of dam safety engineering. Inadequate factors of safety have led to catastrophic failures causing thousands of deaths and billions in damage.
takeaways: Overturning safety factor compares stabilizing and destabilizing moments
Sliding safety factor compares friction resistance to horizontal water force
Minimum factors of safety range from 1.5 to 3.0 depending on load case

faq.question: What is the factor of safety against overturning for a dam?
faq.answer: It is the ratio of the stabilizing moment from the dam's weight to the overturning moment from water pressure, uplift, and other destabilizing forces, all calculated about the downstream toe. Codes typically require a minimum factor of safety of 1.5 for normal loads and 1.

faq.question: How is sliding resistance calculated for a concrete dam on rock?
faq.answer: Sliding resistance equals the net vertical force (dam weight minus uplift) multiplied by the friction coefficient of the dam-foundation contact, plus any cohesion along the interface.
